name: Private Market Valuation
title: Private Market Valuation
answer: Private market valuation is the practice of estimating what a private company or a private asset is worth when no public market price exists. It covers early-stage venture rounds, growth equity, buyouts, fund portfolio marks, secondary transactions, and employee equity such as 409A valuations. In the AI sector, the scope includes startups whose value rests on models, data, compute contracts, and talent rather than only revenue. The work supports fundraising, LP reporting, tax, litigation, and deal negotiation.

sections.body: Private market valuation is the practice of estimating what a private company or a private asset is worth when no public market price exists. It covers early-stage venture rounds, growth equity, buyouts, fund portfolio marks, secondary transactions, and employee equity such as 409A valuations. In the AI sector, the scope includes startups whose value rests on models, data, compute contracts, and talent rather than only revenue. The work supports fundraising, LP reporting, tax, litigation, and deal negotiation.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on financial statements, cap tables, term sheets, data rooms, and market data. Public comparables matter, and the 117 listed AI-related instruments this site tracks with daily prices can serve as a reference point for multiples and volatility. Precedent transactions, including the 355 merger and acquisition filings tracked here, help anchor deal pricing. Valuation teams also use spreadsheets, dedicated valuation platforms, and increasingly cloud data pipelines that pull from accounting, HR, and product systems.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Analysts typically choose among three approaches: market, income, and cost. The market approach uses multiples from comparable public companies and precedent transactions, adjusted for size, growth, and lack of marketability. The income approach projects future cash flows and discounts them, often with scenario or Monte Carlo analysis for uncertain AI adoption curves. Early-stage AI companies may be valued with the venture capital method or an option pricing model tied to milestones. Due diligence checks revenue quality, gross margin after compute costs, data rights, and model defensibility.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Valuation governance covers independence, documentation, audit, and conflict management. Fair value standards such as ASC 820 and IFRS 13 require consistent inputs and disclosure of unobservable assumptions. For AI companies, provenance of training data, ownership of model weights, and exposure to litigation are central risk factors, and the 148 active AI lawsuits tracked here show why. Compliance teams also draw on the 219 compliance and regulation pages on this site to map obligations across jurisdictions. Funds often use valuation committees and limited partner advisory committees to review marks and manage disputes.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Private market valuation is moving toward more frequent marks, greater transparency, and more data-driven processes. AI tools are being applied to comparable selection, document review, and scenario modeling, though human judgment remains central. Secondary markets and continuation funds are creating more price signals for private assets. For AI companies, the horizon depends on proving durable unit economics, clear data rights, and defensible models as public market volatility feeds back into private marks. Regulators and investors are likely to demand more consistent disclosure of valuation inputs and assumptions.
